What are the weather requirements to fly VFR into class B airspace? 3 SM & clear of clouds, 91.155.
What are the weather requirements to fly into class C airspace? 1,000 ft & 3 SM and cloud clearance of 500 below, 1,000 above, and 2,000 horizontal. 91.155 (a), (c), & (d).

What is Special VFR and when may you use it? With ATC clearance and below 10,000 MSL, may land and depart airports in Class B, C, D, & E clear of clouds and 1 mile visibility. 91.157 and Appendix D, section 3.
What is the boundaries, pilot certification, & airplane equipment for Class A airspace? 18,000 to FL600, IFR flight plan, have Two Way Radio contact, a Transponder w/ mode C and an ATC clearance.

What is the boundaries, pilot certification, & airplane equipment for Class B Airspace? Surface to 10,000 feet MSL, nations busiest airports, lateral boundaries variable, Two-way radio, Private pilot (FAR 91 appendix D, sec. 3) or student pilot with endorsement, Transponder w/ mode C, unless otherwise approved by ATC, if IFR, must have VOR, and an ATC clearance.

What is the boundaries, pilot certification, & airplane equipment for Class C Airspace? Surface to 4,000 feet above airport within 5 NM radius charted in MSL. 1,200 feet above surface to 4,000 feet above surface within 10 NM radius charted in MSL, and, normally a 20 NM outer area. Two-way radio, Transponder with Mode C, unless otherwise authorized, and ATC contact.

What is the boundaries, pilot certification, & airplane equipment for Class D Airspace? Surface to 2,500 feet above airport charted in MSL with individually tailored lateral boundaries, a Two-way radio. Without tower in operation, airspace reverts to Class E with controlled airspace from surface or 700 feet AGL -- consult AFD.

What is the boundaries, pilot certification, & airplane equipment for Class E Airspace? Begins at 14,500 MSL unless designated at surface, 700 feet, or 1,200 AGL up to but not including 18,000 feet, may be an airport surface area, extensions of Class B, C, and airspace, transition areas, enroute domestic area, federal airways, and off shore airspace areas out to 12 NM from shore.
What is the boundaries, pilot certification, & airplane equipment for Class G Airspace? All other airspace (uncontrolled)
What is Special Use Airspace? Prohibited areas, Restricted areas, Warning areas, Military Operations Area (MOA), Alert areas, and Controlled firing areas.
What are the minimum safe altitudes? 91.119(a)(b)(c)
What are the VFR cruising altitude rules? 91.159
Can a student pilot fly solo at night? 61.89
What is the minimum visibility for a VFR night flight? 91.155
What airspeed should you use to make you initial climb from an unfamiliar airport at night?
What are the altitudes when oxygen use is required by crew members and passengers? 91.211
What is a minimum equipment list (MEL) and which aircraft require one? 91.213
What is a letter of authorization and where would you obtain one to operate your aircraft without the required equipment? 91.213 (a)(2)
What is a special flight permit? 91.213 (e)
What are Advisory Circulars? AC 61-21 pg 4
Where are the standards for the private and commercial pilot established? PTS
What endorsements must a student have prior to solo? 61.87
What are the minimum Wx conditions a student may solo in? 61.89
For the purposes of student solo flight, what distance is considered cross country? 61.93
Can a student solo in Class B airspace? 61.95, 91.131
What records is an instructor required to keep and for how long? 61.189
What pilot certificate must an airman have in order to charge for their pilot services? Private with stipulations. 61.118.

How may a private pilot with the limitation “night flying prohibited” on his/her certificate get it removed? By flying the required night flight time and make application for a new certificate. 61.109(a)(2).

What class of medical are you required to have for an initial CFI ASEL? Third class. Implication of 61.39 & 61.183 may be misunderstood in that a commercial pilot must have a 2d class, however, 8700.1, vol. II, p. 11-3 states third class.
Are you required to demonstrate spin entry and recovery procedures on this practical? No -- inspector may accept logbook endorsement of this training and instructional ability. 61.183.

If you fail the practical test on the first attempt, would you be required to demonstrate spin entry and recovery procedures on the retake? If the practical was failed due to “deficiencies of knowledge or skill relating to stall awareness, spins, or spin recovery techniques, the applicant must satisfactorily demonstrate both knowledge and skill in these areas on the retake. 61.183(e) & 61.49(b).
Who is responsible for maintaining an aircraft in an airworthy condition? Owner. 91.403(a).
What maintenance inspections must be performed on an aircraft used for hire? 91.409
How would you teach the inportance of a thorough weather check? Safety
What conditions would create a concern for fog developing? AC 61-23 pg 119
What is the definition of ceiling? FAR Part 1

(If CFI Applicant has questions they would like to ask the new student, then I will play that role and they can tell me how they would adjust their lesson plans.) I can play two different people, one a competent smart but very surfer laid back 18 year old, and the other a church going grandmother that doesn’t drive.

Psychological Obstacles: What might they be? Airsickness, fear of crashing or stalls
Ensuring student ability: IE how would you know that a student is safe for first solo? Unassisted flight from start to finish carried out in a safe manner.
PROFESSIONALISM: What are the hallmarks of professionalism?
